_note: Reference for the write-up (PDF). Not loaded by the app.

framing.goal: Make the registry the place a developer goes to decide which MCP server to adopt, not just browse a list.
framing.approach: Keep today's catalog as it is and add a small set of enhancements where the information is thin or wrong. Each enhancement answers one of the five questions from Q1 and fixes a problem found in Q2.
five_questions: Do I trust who runs it?

enhancements.title: Search finds servers by what they do
enhancements.question: Does it do my job?
enhancements.before: Search matches names and providers only. 'seo' misses MetricSpot even though its description says SEO; 'microsoft docs' and 'figma' return nothing although matching servers exist.
enhancements.after: Search also covers descriptions, tool names and tool descriptions, with a small synonym list. All words must match. A row matched through a tool says which tool.
enhancements.evidence: Q2 problem 6 (search and taxonomy). Tool descriptions are available for 655 servers from the direct check.

enhancements.title: Status column and a 'Working now' filter
enhancements.question: Does it work today?
enhancements.before: No status anywhere. A developer finds out a server is down only after trying to connect.
enhancements.after: Each row shows Up, Failing, 'Up · catalog can't connect', or Not checked. Failing servers are hidden by default, not deleted, with a visible 'N hidden' count.
enhancements.evidence: Q2 problem 2: 93 of 680 No Auth servers failed twice minutes apart; 114 of 1,368 failed the direct check twice; 23 work directly but fail through the catalog's own connection.

enhancements.title: Login shows what the server actually did
enhancements.question: Can I connect it safely?
enhancements.before: The auth badge is a hand-entered label. 18 servers labeled No Auth ask for a login when connected; 31 labeled API key actually use OAuth.
enhancements.after: The Login column shows what happened when we connected, with a small checkmark. When the catalog label is wrong, the row shows one red chip: 'Listed as No Auth · needs login'.
enhancements.evidence: Q2 problem 1 (wrong authentication or connection configuration); Exa journey.

enhancements.title: Tools column with risk flags
enhancements.question: Does it do my job? / Can I connect it safely?
enhancements.before: 617 entries show no tools before connecting; nothing says whether a tool can change data or spend money.
enhancements.after: Tool count per row, plus 'can write' or 'can spend money' when relevant. 'After login' when the list is hidden.
enhancements.evidence: Q2 problem 3. 655 servers list tools openly; 305 have tools that can change data; 64 have purchase tools.

enhancements.title: Owner instead of Provider
enhancements.question: Do I trust who runs it?
enhancements.before: 'Provider' is usually just the domain name. 'Google Workspace' (provider: Google) and 'Playwright' (provider: Microsoft) run on TrueFoundry's servers; Postgres and Filesystem are demos.
enhancements.after: Owner column: the verified domain with a checkmark, 'Hosted by TrueFoundry', 'Demo', or 'Unverified'.
enhancements.evidence: Q2 problem 4. 1,327 servers match an Official MCP Registry entry with proven domain or GitHub ownership.

enhancements.title: Cost, only when known
enhancements.question: What will it cost me?
enhancements.before: Cost is invisible or buried in tool descriptions. AgenticTotem is labeled No Auth but charges $0.01 USDC per URL.
enhancements.after: A Cost column shows Free, Free tier, Paid plan or Per call where verified; otherwise a dash.

enhancements.title: More useful server page
enhancements.question: Can I connect it safely?
enhancements.before: Tools are hidden behind 'Connect to view tools' for login servers; no permissions; no config for a client like Cursor.
enhancements.after: Tool descriptions with a tag only for write, destructive or spends-money tools; permissions requested before login (write scopes highlighted); a copy-ready Cursor config and the TrueFoundry Gateway option.
enhancements.evidence: Confluence publishes its OAuth scopes before login, including write:jira-work. 346 servers publish their scopes.

enhancements.title: Compare up to three servers
enhancements.question: All five
enhancements.before: No way to compare; developers open tabs.
enhancements.after: Six rows: status, login, owner, tools, permissions, cost. Only rows that differ are highlighted.
enhancements.evidence: SEO journey: Ahrefs, Abbyseo and MetricSpot differ on login, cost and free path, which today can't be seen side by side.

enhancements.title: 'Same server as' note
enhancements.question: Does it do my job?
enhancements.before: Microsoft Learn appears twice; Confluence and Atlassian share one endpoint.
enhancements.after: A quiet 'Same server as X' line under the name. Nothing is merged or deleted.
enhancements.evidence: Q2 problem 7 and its 'ignore' rule (the two Tandems are different servers).

kept.title: Search box, filter dropdowns, table, sortable headers
kept.why: Familiar and fast; we improve what they contain.

kept.title: Category and auth filters
kept.why: Kept; auth now reflects the check.

kept.title: 'Try it' and the playground
kept.why: The catalog's best feature; every row still links to it.

kept.title: One page per server
kept.why: Same structure, with more decision-relevant detail.

not_added: No overall score or grade: it hides the reason and mixes fresh and stale data.
No GitHub stars or popularity sort: most servers are hosted with no public code, and we have no usage data.
No explanation inside the app: the reasoning lives in the write-up.
